listen_text: Section. Unique Readability. We may wonder if for each term there is a unique way of forming it, and there is. For each lambda term there is only one way to construct and interpret it. In the following discussion, a formation is the procedure of constructing a term using the formation rules (one or several times) of the definition of lambda terms . Lemma. A term starts with either a variable or a parenthesis. End lemma. Proof. Something counts as a term only if it is constructed according to the definition of lambda terms . If it is the result of the variable formation clause , it must be a variable. If it is the result of the abstraction formation clause or the application formation clause , it starts with a parenthesis. End proof. Lemma. The result of an application starts with either two parentheses or a parenthesis and a variable. End lemma. Proof. If capital M is the result of an application, it is of the form the application of capital P to capital Q, end application , so it begins with a parenthesis. Since capital P is a term, by the lemma on the first symbol of a term , it begins either with a parenthesis or a variable. End proof. Lemma. No proper initial part of a term is itself a term. End lemma. Exercise. Prove the lemma that no proper initial part is a term by induction on the length of terms. End exercise. This exercise remains unsolved. Proposition. Unique Readability. There is a unique formation for each term. In other words, if a term capital M is formed by a formation, then it is the only formation that can form this term. End proposition. Proof. We prove this by induction on the formation of terms. List. Next item. capital M is of the form x , where x is some variable. Since the results of abstractions and applications always start with parentheses, they cannot have been used to construct capital M ; Thus, the formation of capital M must be a single step of the definition of lambda terms the variable formation clause . Next item. capital M is of the form lambda x, with body capital N, end abstraction , where x is some variable and capital N is a term. It could not have been constructed according to the definition of lambda terms the variable formation clause , because it is not a single variable. It is not the result of an application, by the lemma on the first symbols of an application . Thus capital M can only be the result of an abstraction on capital N . By inductive hypothesis we know that formation of capital N is itself unique. Next item. capital M is of the form the application of capital P to capital Q, end application , where capital P and capital Q are terms. Since it starts with a parentheses, it cannot also be constructed by the definition of lambda terms the variable formation clause . By the lemma on the first symbol of a term , capital P cannot begin with lambda , so the application of capital P to capital Q, end application cannot be the result of an abstraction. Now suppose there were another way of constructing capital M by application, for example, it is also of the form the application of capital P prime to capital Q prime, end application . Then capital P is a proper initial segment of capital P prime (or vice versa), and this is impossible by the lemma that no proper initial part is a term . So capital P and capital Q are uniquely determined, and by inductive hypothesis we know that formations of capital P and capital Q is unique. End list. End proof. Next item. x , where x is a variable uniquely determined by capital M . Next item. lambda x, with body capital N, end abstraction , where x is a variable and capital N is another term, both of which is uniquely determined by capital M .
